messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache size spike detected on servepool 'us-west-2-gpu-a' for model: open-7b-optimized. metric: kv_cache_entries > 3x baseline over 3m, sustained. autoscaler reports backpressure on batching queue. Paging eng-oncall.
perf-bot: rolling 1m P50/P95: 38ms / 920ms -> 3.1s. request error rate increased from 0.2% -> 1.8%.
sanjay: I'm oncall, taking this. first ask: any recent rollout or config change in the last 30m?
jess: no deploys in the window from infra. saw a config push to continuous-batching window at 12:34 UTC (reduced min_window to 4ms) — linked in config-audit. could be related.
maya: speculative-decoding flags were enabled for this model earlier today to improve tail latency for short responses. might be interacting with KV draft/target logic.
sanjay: hypothesis: speculative decoding is generating divergent drafts causing excessive KV cache churn + continuous batching amplification. we should triage by toggling speculative-decoding off for the affected model and increasing batch backpressure. low-risk rollback first.
luke: CS reports two customers noticing intermittent 5-10s responses for streaming endpoints. ticket #CS-4782, small cohort but high severity for product.
anne: applying temporary runtime knobs: throttling batch window and disabling speculative for canary. will run canary then flip global if stable.
paul: flag priority = P1. customers impacted on hosted API. keep me updated for exec notif.

jess: running canary change now:
```bash
# disable speculative decoding for model in runtime config
redwoodctl config set model/open-7b-optimized.speculative_decoding false --env production --pool us-west-2-gpu-a
# raise max_batch_tokens and add KV evict backpressure
redwoodctl config set runtime.max_batch_tokens 2048 --pool us-west-2-gpu-a
redwoodctl config set kv_cache.evict_threshold 0.75 --pool us-west-2-gpu-a
```

perf-bot: canary metrics (2 minutes after): P95 down to 480ms, error-rate back to 0.45%. kv_cache_entries trending down 60% from peak.
sanjay: good sign. rolling to remainder of pool with staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and 2m observation windows.

maya: reminder: speculative decoding bug we saw last quarter caused target/draft kv mismatch when partial drafts were cached and then overwritten; cache divergence then forced heavier recompute which multiplied under continuous batching. adding this to post-incident notes.
luke: CS: emailed affected customers with note about transient perf blips and mitigation in flight.
paul: action item list:
- root-cause: confirm interaction between speculative_decoding + continuous-batching + kv_cache eviction policy (owner: maya)
- short-term: runtime config revert documented and automated rollback if P95 > 1s during rollout (owner: jess)
- monitoring: add alert for kv_cache entry growth and per-pool speculative-fail metric (owner: anne)
- customer comms: follow up with CS for postmortem message (owner: luke)

jess: rollout completed at 1953218120. final metrics: P95 420ms, error-rate 0.25%, kv_cache back to baseline.
sanjay: handing to oncall rotation next shift — leaving mitigation notes and links to logs. marking incident as mitigated and creating incident ticket INC-2026.
paul: thanks team — prep blameless postmortem and include recommended config safe-guards (e.g., block speculative on models on continuous-batching pools until proven). :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 created. severity: P1 -> mitigated. Timeline and links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026/logs

maya: I'll take the RCA writeup and schedule a follow-up with runtime and ML infra to design a safer rollout path for speculative changes.

sanjay: closing thread, moving to postmortems folder.
